subject: Second order test in mixedmirt function

messages.author: 9480f1551ff24a8b
messages.subject: Second order test in mixedmirt function
parts:
I've been using the mixedmirt function to estimate explanatory IRT models. I've noticed that when I inspect the returned model, the second order test pretty consistently indicates that the model may have converged to a local maximum. This was an issue in my own dataset, but I've noticed I can replicate this issue with the randomly generated example data in mixedmirt. Note that most of this example is copied directly froc for the mixedmirt function. I'm omitting all but the relevant output.

#make some data
set.seed(1234)
N <- 750
a <- matrix(rlnorm(10,.3,1),10,1)
d <- matrix(rnorm(10), 10)
Theta <- matrix(sort(rnorm(N)))
pseudoIQ <- Theta * 5 + 100  + rnorm(N, 0 , 5)
pseudoIQ <- (pseudoIQ - mean(pseudoIQ))/10  #rescale variable for numerical stability
group <- factor(rep(c('G1','G2','G3'), each = N/3))
data <- simdata(a,d,N, itemtype = rep('2PL',10), Theta=Theta)
covdata <- data.frame(group, pseudoIQ)
#use parallel computing
mirtCluster()

#specify IRT model
model <- 'Theta = 1-10'

#model with no person predictors
mod0 <- mirt(data, model, itemtype = 'Rasch')

#group as a fixed effect predictor (aka, uniform dif)
mod1 <- mixedmirt(data, covdata, model, fixed = ~ 0 + group + items)
mod1

Call:
mixedmirt(data = data, covdata = covdata, model = model, fixed = ~0 + 
    group + items)

Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
Converged within 0.001 tolerance after 13 MHRM iterations.
mirt version: 1.31 
M-step optimizer: NR1 
Latent density type: Gaussian 

Information matrix estimated with method: MHRM
Second-order test: model is a possible local maximum
Condition number of information matrix =  173.4366

Log-likelihood = -4041.743, SE = 0.034
Estimated parameters: 40 
AIC = 8109.487; AICc = 8109.982
BIC = 8169.548; SABIC = 8128.268

I experimented with various options to try to eliminate the issue, such as decreasing the tolerance for both the general likelihood and the SEs, increasing the number of draws, and increasing the burn in period. I don't seem to be able to eliminate the error. What's causing this, and are there steps I can take to address this?

I'm aware that I can fit the model that I'm currently using in the mirt function and EM or a different maximization algorithm using the covdata and formula options, and the estimation time isn't an issue.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Second order test in mixedmirt function
parts:
Someone also raised this issue recently, and I believe it is an artifact of Cai's approach to estimating the ACOV. The MHRM method effectively jitters the parameter estimates around the MLE estimates and computes the gradient/Hessian of the complete data solution to form the observed information/ACOV estimate. However, because the MLEs are being jittered there can be some over/underinflation effects, where even unidentified models could appear identified if the stochastic parameters are in a more 'curved' location. Hence, as it turns out, the MHRM ACVOV approach is rather poor at detecting non-identified models. 

The better approach is the use the 'FMHRM' method, which fixes the values at the MLE rather than allowing them to jump around, and gives a Monte Carlo estimate at that location instead. I've found this is much more stable/reasonable, but the cost right now is that it takes longer to compute (it could likely be parallelized though, and when that gets implemented I'll no doubt make the default for the MHRM the 'FMHRM' method instead to avoid problems like this). HTH you understand the issue a little better.

Phil

messages.author: 9480f1551ff24a8b
messages.subject: Re: Second order test in mixedmirt function
parts:
I'm using version 1.31 of the mirt package. The FMHRM method appears to be an option to estimate standard errors only. Also, when fitting an IRT model with covariates, the mirt function doesn't appear to accept FMHRM as an option to calculate SEs, e.g.

mod1a <- mirt(data, model, itemtype = 'Rasch', method = 'MHRM', SE.type = 'FMHRM')
Stage 3 = 16, LL = -5120.3, AR(4.48) = [0.37], gam = 0.0233, Max-Change = 0.0004
mod1a <- mirt(data, model, itemtype = 'Rasch', method = 'MHRM', SE.type = 'FMHRM',
+               covdata = covdata, formula = ~ 0 + group)
Error: method must be from the EM estimation family

So, it sounds like FMHRM would be your preferred estimation method, but this isn't implemented yet for latent regression (aka explanatory IRT) models. Does this sound correct? If so, I think I shall default to using EM methods for my current purposes.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Second order test in mixedmirt function
parts:
I think the rule of thumb here is use the EM algorithm until it is no longer feasible. Relying on stochastic approximations is fine, but after all they are only approximations to the solution rather than exact like those provided by quasi-Newton methods and the EM. Also, to make your code work just use the variant in the mixedmirt() function, which is more dedicated to this process (the mirt() function should throw a better error in this regard). 

Phil
